eventMetadata.context_description:
**Southern Utah holds a modest edge as the 59% favorite in this non-conference Beehive Bowl matchup on September 5 in Cedar City, reflecting its home-field advantage and greater roster continuity entering the teams’ first meeting since 2021.**

Southern Utah returns to the Big Sky after two 7-5 seasons and opened 2026 with a competitive 21-28 loss at No. 2 Montana, where the Thunderbirds generated 510 total yards and 83 plays behind dual-threat QB Will Burns (24-of-34 passing, 251 yards, 1 TD; 119 rushing yards). The team’s recent emphasis on spreading the ball and building on prior FCS-leading rushers supports expectations for a balanced attack at Eccles Coliseum. Weber State, under first-year head coach Eric Kjar and with roughly 80 new players, opened with a 30-29 road win at Northern Colorado but dealt with multiple injuries, including a dislocated finger to starting QB Devin Brown and issues for several skill players and linemen. The Wildcats face a quick turnaround on the road against a familiar in-state rival where they have historically dominated (21-8 series lead) but enter with transition-related uncertainty. Trader consensus appears driven by SUU’s stability and venue edge offsetting Weber State’s narrow recent result.
